title.narrative: Girls Empowerment and Quality Education for All Project

description.narrative: The Girls Empowerment and Quality Education for All (P169222) would be financed through a proposed IDA grant in the amount of US$15 million and a proposed GPE grant in the amount of US$2.2 million, using an Investment Project Financing (IPF) lending instrument. The Project aims to address the challenges of supporting a more conducive learning environment for girls empowerment, system-wide activities to tackle the learning poverty and reaching the most vulnerable. The scope of the Project is general education (covering preschool throughout secondary education), but each component would focus on different levels of education to achieve the development objectives.
The Project Development Objective are to equip girls with life skills and improve student learning outcomes for all.

title.narrative: Girls improving life skills under the project

comment.narrative: Percentage of girls improving life skills under the project. The improvement in life skills will be measured based on pre and post assessments of the beneficiaries of Subcomponent 1.1 interventions. The life skills that will be prioritized for girls' empowerment are those that raise aspirations and foster agency to take control over life choices, such as financial literacy, knowledge about SRH, and self-confidence. Pre-tests were applied for the first time in April 2023 during the pilot phase. The scaled up imlementation started in October 2023 and pre-tests were applied to beneficiaries in November 2023. Post tests were applied in July 2024, with data under analysis. In total, 1316 students in grades 10-12 participated in one of the 75 clubs established, out of which 865 were girls.

title.narrative: Girls improving life skills under the project

comment.narrative: Percentage of girls improving life skills under the project. The improvement in life skills will be measured based on pre and post assessments of the beneficiaries of Subcomponent 1.1 interventions. The life skills that will be prioritized for girls' empowerment are those that raise aspirations and foster agency to take control over life choices, such as financial literacy, knowledge about SRH, and self-confidence. For the 2023/24 school year, there were 1500 students enrolled in the boys' and girls' clubs. The attendance rate was 88 percent, where 1316 students in grades 10-12 participated in one of the 75 clubs established, out of which 865 were girls. However, the participation rates in the pre and post assessments were low, respectively at 39 and 56 percent, with limited overlap between the students that participated in both tests. For those students who participated in both tests, 66 percent registered improvements in life skills. For 2024/25, 1700 have participated in the clubs.

title.narrative: Teachers trained under the project who demonstrated improved teaching practices in the classroom

comment.narrative: The ratio between number of teachers that demonstrate better teaching practices in the classroom, and number of teachers who received training in literacy and numeracy under the project. The classroom observation will use the TEACH instrument. The baseline is the TEACH application from February 2022, where only 14.2 percent of teachers were performing at the satisfactory level. Targets therefore represent the proportion of teachers trained that are scoring in the satisfactory category. To meet the end of project target, the number would need to be at least 30.2 percent (14.2 + 16). A new round of TEACH was applied in November 2024 and data is under analysis.

Percentage of girls with career aspirations to start tertiary education after graduating secondary education. The data compiled for the second round will provide more clarity on the impact of the clubs on girls' career aspirations.

title.narrative: Completion rate in secondary education (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative: This PDO indicator was upgraded from an intermediate indicator during the project restructuring. The completion rate for secondary education is a better, more stable indicator of improving student learning, and success for keeping girls in school more generally, than reductions in dropouts, which vary widely from year to year in Sao Tome and Principe. According to the 2022/23 education statistical bulletin, completion rates for students in secondary education increased to 57 percent compared to 51 percent in the previous school calendar year. This information will be updated after the 2023/24 statistical bulletin becomes available.

The completion rate for secondary education is a better, more stable indicator of improving student learning, and success for keeping girls in school more generally, than reductions in dropouts, which vary widely from year to year in Sao Tome and Principe. According to the 2022/23 education statistical bulletin, completion rates for students in secondary education increased to 57 percent compared to 51 percent in the previous school calendar year.

title.narrative: Students benefiting from direct interventions to enhance learning

comment.narrative: Students participating in PASEC, ALLEB, and ALLES are all considered as beneficiaries of activities to enhance learning. As such, the indicator for July 2024 is 19,200. The gender breakdown is not yet available.

title.narrative: Large-scale learning assessments completed at the primary or secondary levels

comment.narrative: Number of national learning assessments (AALEB and AALES) and international learning assessment (PASEC) completed. PASEC will be considered completed when reports are received and results disseminated.

This indicator refers to preschool teachers who received in-service training and basic education teachers trained in literacy and numeracy through structured training under the project. The gender breakdown is not yet available.

title.narrative: Number of grievances received and addressed through the project the GRM system

comment.narrative: This indicator tracks the number of grievances received and addressed using the grievance redressal mechanisms that currently exist or will be established. A total of 25 complaints have been received, 6 of these complaints are using the GRM from the project. None are project-related, but rather school-related (outside the scope of the project).

title.narrative: Grade 2 students who have improved grade-level competencies in numeracy

comment.narrative: Percentage of grade 2 students who have grade-level competencies in numeracy in the PASEC student assessment. Baseline data is the round of PASEC applied in 2022 (53.70 percent). The second round of PASEC is expected to be applied in 2025. Data to be reported when PASEC results received.

title.narrative: Carry out PASEC, analyze results and disseminate findings

comment.narrative: PASEC was carried out in 2022 for the 2nd and 6th grades. The PASEC 2022 report was published and results have been disseminated to the school community. The next round of PASEC will be carried out in 2025, for the 2nd, 6th and 9th grades.

Carry out beneficiary survey. The beneficiary survey will be incorporated to the AALEB and AALES students and teachers socioeconomic questionnaires. The next round of the AALEB and AALES is scheduled for 2025.
